title: Rate-controlled Cryopreservation and Thawing of Mammalian Cells
protocol: Maintain cells in an actively growing state prior to freezing.
Harvest cells gently using the same method as routine subculture.
Use a laminar flow hood for cell handling.
Prepare cryovials at <-4°C using a CoolBox CFT30 ice-free system.
Prepare freezing medium containing 90% serum and 10% glycerol.
Store prepared freezing medium at 2° to 8°C until use.
Mix 50% cell-conditioned medium with 50% fresh medium containing either 10% glycerol or 10% DMSO.
Determine the total number of cells and viability using a hemacytometer or cell counter and Trypan Blue exclusion.
Calculate the required volume of freezing medium based on the desired viable cell density, typically allowing for 1 ml per vial.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at approximately 100–200 × g for 5 to 10 minutes.
Aseptically decant the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet and resuspend the cell pellet in cryoprotective freezing medium to achieve a final concentration of 2 to 4 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Label each cryovial with detailed information about its contents.
Place labeled cryovials into the CoolRack CFT30 within the CoolBox CFT30 ice-free cooling station.
Aliquot 1 ml of cell suspension in freezing medium into each cryovial, ensuring frequent gentle mixing for a homogeneous suspension.
Freeze cells at a rate of -1°C/min using a CoolCell® alcohol-free cell freezing container in a -80°C freezer or dry ice locker.
Place the solid core of the CoolCell at room temperature and seat it in the bottom of the central cavity.
Ensure sample vials containing 1 ml of cell suspension are placed in each well without extending above the CoolCell body.
Make sure all chambers within the CoolCell, including “blank” vials, contain an equal volume of media to ensure radially symmetric cooling.
Fully seal the lid on the CoolCell.
Place the sealed CoolCell into a -80°C freezer or dry ice locker with at least 1 inch of free space clearance around it.
Store the CoolCell container in a -80°C freezer for at least 4 hours and up to 24 hours before transferring to permanent storage.
Transfer cells to permanent storage using dry ice to maintain low temperatures and prevent cell damage.
Test cell viability by thawing one vial after short term storage in gas phase nitrogen before the stock culture is terminated.

Record information about cells in the repository including culture identity, passage or population doubling level, date frozen, freezing medium and method used, number of cells per vial, total number of vials initially frozen and remaining, their locations, expected viability, and results of quality control tests.
Remove a vial from its storage location using appropriate safety equipment and place it into the CoolRack CFT30.
Transfer the CoolRack to a 37°C water bath immediately with a ThermalTray HP underneath for stabilization.
Place cryovials into a laminar flow hood before opening.
Wipe the outside of the vial with 70% ethanol.
Remove cryoprotective agents quickly and gently from thawed cells.
Transfer pre-warmed complete growth medium into the centrifuge tube containing thawed cells.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at approximately 200 × g for 5–10 minutes.
Check the clarity of supernatant and visibility of a complete pellet after centrifugation.
Aseptically decant the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Gently resuspend the cells in fresh growth medium.
Transfer the resuspended cells into the appropriate culture vessel.
